sources.locator: Primary: introduction and Sub-Stat table (Base, Effective, Displayed, Bonus, Penalty)

rules.behavior: effective = integer_part(base) + bonus - penalty. Base remains fractional. Displayed equals effective without delusion; it is a separate perceived value. Unqualified engine stat references mean effective.
rules.precision_rounding: Take integer part of base before modifiers; negative-value rounding and storage precision unknown.
rules.bounds: unknown: clamps and overflow behavior are not established by this section.
rules.trigger_cadence: When an effective stat is needed; exact recomputation cadence unknown.
rules.update_order: Integer part of base, then add bonus and subtract penalty; ordering among modifier sources unknown.

implementation.notes: effective_speed() uses integer fields and an extra minimum-zero clamp. Full seven-stat model and delusion display are absent; existing clamp is not source evidence.

outputs.name: walking_rate
outputs.unit: relative walking units; absolute distance/time scale unknown

rules.behavior: walking_rate = min(36, ((effective_speed + 5) div 6) * 2). Initial base Speed is 13 and initial walking rate is 6.
rules.precision_rounding: Integer division before multiplication, consistent with the explicitly stated initial rate 6 at Speed 13. Negative operands unknown.
rules.trigger_cadence: Derived from effective Speed; recomputation cadence unknown.
rules.update_order: Add 5, integer divide by 6, multiply by 2, cap at 36.

implementation.notes: walking_speed() implements the nonnegative rate formula; effective_speed() upstream adds an unverified clamp. Absolute travel scale belongs to MOVE-002.

inputs.name: walking_rate
inputs.unit: reconstruction walking units per real second

rules.behavior: For positive rate, tile_duration = 6 / walking_rate; advance_travel adds real_seconds * walking_rate / 6 to tile progress. The same calibration applies to City and Dungeon.
rules.precision_rounding: Floating-point travel progress; arrival clamps progress to 1. Zero rate prevents travel; tile_travel_seconds uses max(1, rate) as a helper safeguard, not an actual zero-rate duration.
rules.bounds: Six units per tile; committed progress capped at 1.
rules.trigger_cadence: Each travel update while a tile step is active.
rules.update_order: Advance progress, then commit the destination at completion.

implementation.notes: Reconstruction calibration only; not measured ST or verified 8-bit Dungeon distance.

questions.question: Can original tile timing be measured separately for ST City and 8-bit Dungeon?

rules.rationale: Six units per tile gives the starting rate 6 a one-real-second stride. Reusing it in Dungeon is a shared remake policy, not original Dungeon evidence.

sources.locator: Time Span: ordinary rate and Ingame / Real correspondence table

rules.behavior: Ordinary unpaused game time runs at 15 game seconds per real second: game_minutes = real_seconds / 4. Source durations default to game time unless specified.
rules.precision_rounding: Preserve fractional game minutes; original accumulator precision unknown.
rules.bounds: Applicable to ordinary elapsed time; calendar bounds not applicable to conversion.
rules.trigger_cadence: Continuous ordinary unpaused passage of time; service acceleration excluded.
rules.update_order: Conversion known; ordering relative to metabolism and other scheduled systems unknown.

implementation.notes: advance_real_seconds() retains minute_fraction and advances whole minutes. Source pause situations, calendar and accelerated service reconciliation remain S03 work.

sources.locator: Entity: +Offset Effects; Effect: introductory paragraphs and +01.b Active index

rules.behavior: An entity holds zero or more effect definitions. Activation copies a definition to the active list. Active index initially FF becomes its own active-list index; initially 00 becomes the previous entity effect active index, usually linking text to a preceding non-text effect.
rules.precision_rounding: Discrete records and byte index descriptions; stable runtime identifiers are not specified.
rules.bounds: Zero or more definitions; active-list capacity unknown.
rules.update_order: Previous-effect linkage is documented; other allocation/update ordering unknown.

implementation.notes: S29 non-timed copy/link lifecycle implemented. Definitions, owners and active copies are distinct; FF/00 group behavior, snapshots and scoped removal tested. Stable session identities are reconstruction architecture; native slot capacity/layout, timer state and saves are excluded.

sources.locator: Entity: +02.b Events; Effect: introduction, +02.b Allow multiple & Required events, +03.b Counter, +04.w Timer, +06.w Interval, +08.b Probability of natural cure

rules.behavior: Set entity events are handled then cleared. Events are forwarded to definitions: opposing-event active effects are removed and listeners are activated by copying. Known events A-E are Get, Drop, Use (& Cast), Unuse, Delete. With effect flag H set, equality compares Type/Interval/ProbToRemove/Action/Offset/NbBlocks/Gab/Param; a match prevents activation of the current and all following effects. This is an activation check, not a general stacking rule.
rules.precision_rounding: Bit flags and discrete records. Timer/interval units unknown. Counter 0 means never removed by execution; finite counter counts executions before deactivation.
rules.bounds: Multiplicity conditional on flag H; other limits unknown.
rules.trigger_cadence: Event handling; timer reaching zero decreases counter and executes effect, then timer restarts using interval. Natural cure is checked on execution; initial timer may differ from interval.
rules.update_order: Source describes opposing removal then listener activation, but exact event-bit priority, simultaneous events, cure/execution/deactivation order and full opposing-event mapping are unknown.

implementation.notes: S29 event portion implemented for generic owners: Get/Drop/Use/Unuse/terminal Delete, held guard, explicit owner-scoped opposition and global H-tail suppression. Unknown bits/Delete listeners rejected. Timer/cure/action fields in this broader rule remain S30 work, so overall coverage stays partial. No gameplay or save hook.
